fixes.explanation: A stranger at the door? Friend, that would've been a much easier conversation for Esau. Isaac says, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.” (Genesis 27:35) It was family, and I think that's the part that stung. Nobody else in that tent is named.

A servant with a dish? Now THAT would be a plot twist. Isaac doesn't go there, though. He says, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.” (Genesis 27:35) The dish was part of the scene, but Isaac points at the person, and the person is Esau's own brother.

I get why you went there, a green plain sounds like a nice consolation prize. But Isaac says, “…your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land, away from the dew of heaven above.” (Genesis 27:39) Not a word about the Jordan. I think Esau was hoping for a softer landing than that, and he doesn't get one in this line.

Milk and honey, baker? That's a premium listing, and Esau doesn't get it here. Isaac says, “…your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land…” (Genesis 27:39) It's the opposite of that picture. The richness is exactly what's missing from his words.

Flock sounds peaceful, like a quiet life with sheep. Isaac's words are much rougher. He says, “You shall live by the sword and serve your brother.” (Genesis 27:40) Then he adds a turn: “But when you rebel, you will tear his yoke from your neck.” (Genesis 27:40) That last part is where the line stops being only heavy.
